subject: ist-f
title: (R)IST.F.------MT.INFO.
description: Diagram in NYM-26, paired with v1-p392-1. (R)IST-F — the reality of isolated focus — is crossed with MT-INFO (music information). The diagram is hub-shaped: IST-F is the central hub, with five upstreams converging on it (MT-INFO, CR-INFO-DY (circular information dynamics), INFO-F (information focus), INTL (intellectualism), CULT-INFO-B (culture information basis)) and one output (IST-S-ALGN, isolated systematic alignment). A separate sub-chain runs DYM-F (dynamic functionalism) → MTH (methodology) → P-FC (particular focus) → CULT-INFO-B (which then feeds back into IST-F). Structural argument: the reality of isolated focus is over-determined by *five* parallel upstreams converging on a single node, and produces only one output — isolated systematic alignment. The dynamic-functionalism → methodology → particular-focus → culture-information-basis chain feeds the isolated focus from one of those five directions, but also produces a recursive loop where culture-information-basis feeds isolated focus, which produces isolated systematic alignment, which is the structural alignment by which isolation gets institutionally recognized. The diagram thus diagrams the post-Ayler structural problem of isolated focus: it requires five different kinds of upstream pressure (musical-info, circular-info-dynamics, info-focus, intellectualism, culture-info-basis), and produces only systematic isolation as its output — not breakthrough. The diagram is Braxton's structural acknowledgment of why the post-Ayler movement remained 'under the underground.'
